subject: Chemistry
prompt: SN2 reaction proceeds with inversion of configuration
explain: SN2 is a backside attack giving complete inversion (Walden inversion).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Order of reactivity of alkyl halides in SN1
explain: SN1 rate depends on carbocation stability: 3° > 2° > 1°.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Order of reactivity of alkyl halides in SN2
explain: SN2 is hindered by bulky groups; least hindered reacts fastest.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Leaving group ability order among halogens
explain: Weaker the base, better the leaving group; I⁻ is weakest base among halides.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Reactivity order of alkyl halides: R–X bond strength
explain: C–F bond is strongest; bond energy decreases down the group.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Finkelstein reaction converts R–Cl/Br to
explain: R–Cl + NaI (acetone) → R–I + NaCl; NaCl precipitates driving equilibrium.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Swarts reaction converts R–Cl to
explain: R–Cl + AgF (or SbF₃) → R–F; used to prepare alkyl fluorides.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Reaction of R–X with KCN gives mainly
explain: CN⁻ is ambident; C-attack dominates giving alkyl cyanide (nitrile).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Reaction of R–X with AgCN gives mainly
explain: AgCN is covalent; N-end attacks giving isocyanide (isonitrile).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Reaction of R–X with KNO₂ gives mainly
explain: KNO₂: O-attack dominates giving alkyl nitrite; AgNO₂ gives nitroalkane.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Wurtz reaction reagent and product type
explain: Wurtz reaction couples two alkyl halides using Na to give a symmetrical alkane.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Grignard reagent formula
explain: Grignard reagent R–MgX forms when R–X reacts with Mg in anhydrous ether.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Nucleophilic substitution on haloarenes requires
explain: EWG stabilize Meisenheimer complex intermediate, facilitating SNAr.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Halogen in haloarenes shows which effect on ring?
explain: Halogen donates lone pair to ring (+M) but withdraws inductively (−I).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Halogens in haloarenes are o/p directors in EAS because of
explain: Despite −I, +M effect directs electrophile to ortho/para positions.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Dipole moment order: CH₃F, CH₃Cl, CH₃Br, CH₃I
explain: Electronegativity dominates over bond length; F most electronegative gives highest μ.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Boiling point order among isomeric alkyl halides (same formula)
explain: Branching reduces surface area and van der Waals forces, lowering boiling point.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which alkyl halide does NOT undergo SN2?
explain: Neopentyl halide is 1° but extreme steric hindrance makes SN2 essentially impossible.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Dehydrohalogenation of 2-bromobutane follows
explain: E2 elimination with strong base gives more substituted (stable) alkene per Saytzeff.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: E2 elimination is favoured by
explain: Bulky strong base and heat favour E2; 3° substrate has most β-H and less SN2 competition.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: DDT is a persistent organic pollutant made from
explain: DDT = dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane; synthesised from chlorobenzene and CCl₃CHO.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Chloroform (CHCl₃) stored with ethanol to prevent
explain: CHCl₃ oxidises in air to toxic phosgene; ethanol acts as stabiliser/scavenger.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: The IUPAC name of CHCl₃ is
explain: CHCl₃ = trichloromethane; 'chloroform' is its common name.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Freons (CFCs) are used as refrigerants; example
explain: Freon-12 (CCl₂F₂) is a common CFC refrigerant; depletes ozone layer.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Victor Meyer test: primary alkyl halide gives colour
explain: 1° R–X → nitroso compound → red with FeCl₃/H₂SO₄ in Victor Meyer test.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: SN1 reaction proceeds with which stereochemical outcome?
explain: SN1 forms planar carbocation; nucleophile attacks both faces giving racemic mixture.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Polarity order of C–X bond (bond polarity, not dipole moment)?
explain: Electronegativity decreases F>Cl>Br>I, so C–F bond is most polar.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Reaction of R–X with AgNO₂ gives mainly?
explain: AgNO₂ is covalent; N-end attacks giving nitroalkane (unlike KNO₂ which also gives nitrite).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Wurtz-Fittig reaction is used to prepare?
explain: Wurtz-Fittig couples aryl halide + alkyl halide with Na to give alkylarene.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Fittig reaction couples two aryl halides with Na to give?
explain: Fittig reaction: 2 ArX + 2Na → Ar–Ar + 2NaX (symmetrical biaryl).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: The C–X bond length order among haloalkanes is?
explain: Bond length increases with atomic size of halogen: F smallest, I largest.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which substrate undergoes SN1 fastest?
explain: Tertiary carbocation is most stable; tert-alkyl halide reacts fastest in SN1.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: In E1 elimination, the rate-determining step involves?
explain: E1: slow ionisation to carbocation (rate-determining), then fast proton loss.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Iodoform (CHI₃) reaction with alkyl halide: CHI₃ forms from?
explain: Iodoform test/reaction: CH₃CH₂X (or CH₃CHO) oxidised and halogenated with I₂/NaOH gives CHI₃.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Nucleophilicity order in polar aprotic solvent?
explain: In polar aprotic solvent, larger/more polarisable halide is better nucleophile: I⁻ best.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Nucleophilicity order in polar protic solvent?
explain: In protic solvent, F⁻ least solvated → strongest nucleophile; order reverses vs aprotic.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Benzyl chloride (C₆H₅CH₂Cl) preferentially undergoes?
explain: Benzylic carbocation is resonance-stabilised, strongly favouring SN1 pathway.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Allylic halides show high SN1 reactivity because?
options: Allylic C–X bond is very strong
explain: Allylic cation delocalises charge over two carbons via resonance, stabilising intermediate.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: What is the product of R–X with NH₃ (excess)?
explain: Alkyl halide + excess NH₃ → primary amine via nucleophilic substitution (Gabriel method preferred for pure amine).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used to prepare?
explain: Gabriel synthesis uses phthalimide + R–X then hydrolysis; gives only primary amines.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which reagent converts R–OH to R–X with inversion (SN2)?
explain: SOCl₂/pyridine proceeds via SN2 on the chlorosulfite ester giving inversion at chiral centre.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: The boiling point order of mono-haloalkanes (same carbon) is?
explain: Boiling point rises with molecular mass and polarisability: R–I has highest van der Waals forces.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Haloarenes are less reactive than haloalkanes in nucleophilic substitution because?
options: Halogens on arenes are better leaving groups
C–X bond has partial double bond character
explain: Lone pair of X delocalises into ring; C–X has double-bond character making it shorter and stronger.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: In electrophilic aromatic substitution, halogens on benzene ring are?
explain: Halogens withdraw by induction (deactivating) but donate by resonance (+M) → o/p-directing.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) on chlorobenzene is facilitated by?
explain: EWG (–NO₂) at o/p stabilise Meisenheimer complex, accelerating SNAr on haloarenes.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: The Meisenheimer complex is an intermediate in?
explain: Meisenheimer complex: anionic σ-complex formed when nucleophile adds to activated haloarene.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Chlorobenzene on reaction with Mg in dry ether gives?
explain: Haloarenes react with Mg in dry ether to form aryl Grignard reagents (ArMgX).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Victor Meyer test: secondary alkyl halide gives which colour?
explain: Secondary RX → secondary nitroalkane → blue colour with Victor Meyer test (nitrous acid + FeSO₄/H₂SO₄).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which of these is a gem-dihalide (same carbon)?
explain: Gem-dihalide: both halogens on same C. CH₃CHCl₂ is 1,1-dichloroethane (gem). ClCH₂CH₂Cl is vicinal.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Density of haloalkanes compared to water?
options: Fluoroalkanes lighter; Cl/Br/I alkanes denser than water
explain: R–F and R–Cl (lower) may be lighter; R–Br and R–I are generally denser than water.
